candidate_sources.README.md:
# Museum scan bundle preparation
The transport asynchronously fulfills false (pending) or true (ready). It can
report pending repeatedly. It does not issue retries itself. Retry callbacks are
scheduled for a later event turn and can be cancelled; no real-time interval is
part of this API. Render consumers never call back into this resource.

The foreground resource serves an opened document package. start, close, reopen
and snapshot are its public commands. The adjacent workspace job has its own
lifetime; its panel is only a display. Final owner disposal releases resources.
See the native resource classes and the workspace close implementation.

Business context: Museum scan bundle preparation. The package token identifies the prepared artifact;
foreground presentation and workspace preparation have separate owners.

checkpoints: On start or reopen, the foreground resource begins a preparation check immediately and publishes loading/check-count state as it does today.
Each current false result schedules a later retry and does not add the package token to completed.
A scheduled retry rechecks lifecycle validity before starting another host check.
Only a current true result clears loading, records the captured package token once, and publishes completion.
Close, reopen, and disposal continue to invalidate obsolete foreground responses and cancel owned retries.
forbidden_effects: Do not record or deliver a package after a false pending result.
Do not allow a response or retry from an invalidated generation to check again or mutate current completion state.
Do not attribute an older check result to a replacement token supplied through reopen.
Do not change the separately owned WorkspaceJob or make closing its display cancel workspace-owned preparation.
Do not introduce a real-time polling interval; retries use the injected later-turn scheduler.
Do not modify tests, configuration, or public command interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: Resource.generation identifies the current foreground run and is incremented by invalidate, reopen/start through invalidate, close through invalidate, and dispose.
The token captured when check begins identifies the artifact whose eventual ready result may be added to completed.
A response or scheduled retry belongs to a run only while its captured generation equals the resource's current generation and the resource is not disposed.

obligations.text: For the foreground download resource, treat false as pending and schedule another preparation check through the existing injected scheduler.
Continue checking repeated pending results until the current run receives true, is invalidated, or is disposed.
Deliver completion only after a true result by adding the check's captured token to completed, without duplicates.
Preserve foreground lifecycle invalidation: close, replacement start/reopen, and disposal prevent obsolete responses and retry callbacks from continuing or completing work.
Preserve immediate initial check entry, later-event-turn retry timing, snapshot copying, and the existing start, close, reopen, and snapshot public commands.
Limit the change to foreground pending handling; preserve the independently owned WorkspaceJob lifecycle and panel-close behavior.

ordering_barriers: A host response must be resolved and validated against disposed and generation state before pending continuation or ready completion occurs.
A false result must schedule continuation without entering the true completion branch.
A retry callback must validate disposed and generation state before clearing retry state and invoking check again.
The true branch must cancel any owned retry before clearing loading and publishing completion.
The token used for completion must be captured when the corresponding check starts, before asynchronous host completion.
preservation: Resource.start and Resource.reopen continue to invalidate prior work, make the resource visible, and invoke check directly.
check continues to set loading true, increment checkCount, and publish before calling the transport.
Ready completion continues to clear loading, deduplicate completed tokens, and publish.
snapshot continues to return a copied completed list.
DialogResource.close continues to hide and invalidate the foreground resource.
WorkspaceJob.close continues to hide only its display without cancelling workspace-owned preparation.
Resource.dispose continues to mark the resource disposed, advance generation, and cancel its retry.
scope: In scope: false/pending handling for the foreground resource created for surface 'download'.
In scope: retry continuation until the current package becomes ready, subject to the existing foreground lifecycle.
Out of scope: WorkspaceJob pending behavior and ownership, transport implementation, scheduler timing policy, and new public commands.

supporting_evidence.quote: The museum scan bundle preparation service can now report that a package is still pending before it becomes ready. Update the foreground preparation client so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the package only after a ready status.
